STRUCTURE:
- Single HTML file, valid doctype, head with title, style block, body with one centered 800x800 <canvas id="canvas">, and a script block at the end.
- Include dat.gui via CDN script tag: https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/dat-gui/0.7.9/dat.gui.min.js (only allowed external library).
- No other external libs/assets/images.

PAGE LAYOUT:
- html/body: margin 0, height 100%, background #05070f (page background), display flex center content vertically and horizontally, min-height 100vh.
- Canvas: width=800 height=800, centered, with a subtle box-shadow / glow border using the background glow color #101a3a and main branch color #00e5ff, border-radius small, positioned centered via flexbox.
- dat.gui panel appears in its default top-right fixed position (leave default dat.gui styling, don't fight it, just make sure it's visible over the dark page).

COLOR PALETTE (use exactly, as JS variables and CSS where relevant):
- background: '#05070f'
- backgroundGlow: '#101a3a'
- branchColor: '#00e5ff'
- accentColor: '#d6ff00'
- synapseColor: '#ff2bd6'
- pulseColor: '#fff36a'
- uiColor: '#ffd400'
- gridColor: 'rgba(0, 229, 255, 0.08)'

JAVASCRIPT ARCHITECTURE (vanilla JS, no modules, plain <script> at bottom, wrapped in an IIFE):
1. SETUP section: get canvas + ctx, set canvas.width/height = 800, define a `params` object holding all tunable values with sensible defaults:
   neuronCount (3-6, default 5, int), growthSpeed (default 1.2, range 0.1-5), maxDepth (default 9, int range 3-14), splitChance (default 0.35, range 0-1), curvature (default 0.6, range 0-2), maxBranchLength (default 90, range 20-200), synapseDistance (default 26, range 5-80), synapseGlow (default 18, range 0-40), pulseSpeed (default 0.02, range 0.001-0.1), pulseFrequency (default 0.6, range 0-3, meaning avg new pulses per second), pulseBrightness (default 1.0, range 0.2-2), backgroundColor '#05070f', branchColor '#00e5ff', accentColor '#d6ff00', synapseColor '#ff2bd6', pulseColor '#fff36a', paused=false.
   Also define maxTotalBranches (e.g. 700) as an internal safety cap, not necessarily a GUI control, to bound recursion/array growth.

2. GUI SETUP section: create `const gui = new dat.GUI();` with four folders exactly named 'Growth', 'Synapses', 'Pulses', 'Visuals'.
   - Growth folder: neuronCount, growthSpeed, maxDepth, splitChance, curvature, maxBranchLength, plus a button 'Regenerate Network' that resets/rebuilds the whole network, and a button 'Clear Canvas' that empties all branches/synapses/pulses (but keeps sim from crashing — regenerate should still work after clear), and a button 'Pause / Resume' that toggles params.paused and also toggles animation loop state. (You can put the 3 buttons in Growth folder as a natural place for global actions, or spread logically, but ensure all 3 buttons exist somewhere in the GUI, each in a fitting folder — regenerate & clear make sense in Growth, pause/resume can go in Visuals or Growth; use your best judgement but ALL THREE BUTTONS MUST EXIST.)
   - Synapses folder: synapseDistance, synapseGlow.
   - Pulses folder: pulseSpeed, pulseFrequency, pulseBrightness.
   - Visuals folder: backgroundColor, branchColor, accentColor, synapseColor, pulseColor (all as dat.gui color controllers using addColor, wired via onChange to update the internal palette variables used by rendering), and it's fine to add the pause/resume button here instead if preferred.
   - Open all folders by default.

3. NEURON GROWTH section: a Branch/segment data model — plain objects, e.g. {x1,y1,x2,y2 (or a mid control point for quadratic curve), angle, depth, length, width, growProgress (0..1), fromNeuronId, tipX, tipY, alive, colorMix (0..1 to blend between branchColor and accentColor for variety)}.
   - `createNetwork()`: clears arrays, picks a random count (3 to 6, or use params.neuronCount) of seed neuron origin points scattered near canvas center (e.g. within ~150px radius of 400,400), each spawns 1-2 initial branch segments with random initial angle.
   - Growth is animated step by step each frame: each active/growing branch has growProgress that increases by params.growthSpeed * deltaFactor each frame; once growProgress reaches 1, the branch tip becomes 'settled', and probabilistically (params.splitChance) spawns 1-2 child branches continuing in a similar-but-slightly-randomized direction (organic curvature via a random angle delta and a quadratic bezier control point offset using params.curvature), with depth+1, until params.maxDepth is reached or maxTotalBranches cap hit or length exceeds params.maxBranchLength budget along that lineage. Randomly vary segment width slightly (e.g. 0.8-1.6 base). Occasionally (smaller probability) spawn an extra thin short side-branch. When no branch is actively growing anymore (all either settled-terminal or capped), mark network as 'stable' (growthDone = true) — stop spawning new branches, but keep everything else animating.

4. SYNAPSE DETECTION section: `checkSynapses()` runs periodically (e.g. every N frames, not necessarily every single frame, for performance) — compare tip positions (or settled terminal tip positions) of branches from DIFFERENT origin neurons (avoid connecting a branch to itself/same neuron trivially, though connecting same-neuron distant branches is acceptable too—prioritize different neurons), if distance < params.synapseDistance create a synapse object {aBranchId/aX/aY, bBranchId/bX/bY, strength, pulsePhase} — before creating, check a Set/map of existing pairs (using sorted branch id pair key) to prevent duplicates. Keep total synapse count bounded (e.g. cap ~120) for performance — stop checking new pairs once cap reached, or just skip creating extra ones silently.

5. PULSE ANIMATION section: maintain an array of active pulses, each referencing a synapse (or a path along a branch chain from neuron to neuron), with `t` (0..1 progress along the path) that increases by params.pulseSpeed * deltaFactor each frame using smooth interpolation (linear or eased) along the quadratic path between the two endpoints; when t>=1 remove pulse (or reverse/recycle). New pulses spawn randomly on existing synapses at a rate driven by params.pulseFrequency (probabilistic per frame based on deltaTime so it's framerate independent, e.g. Math.random() < pulseFrequency*dt) — pick a random existing synapse to fire a pulse, so different paths light up over time. Also, DURING growth (before growthDone), branch tips themselves can show a small traveling glow at the growth front (that's already covered by growProgress rendering) — pulses on synapses should mainly happen once synapses exist (they can appear as soon as a synapse forms, even mid-growth).

6. RENDERING section: `render()` called each animation frame:
   - Clear/fill background with backgroundColor.
   - Draw a soft radial background glow at canvas center using backgroundGlow color (#101a3a) blended subtly (e.g. large radial gradient, low alpha).
   - Draw a faint grid or scanline pattern using gridColor (rgba(0,229,255,0.08)) — e.g. horizontal scanlines every few px, or a sparse grid, very subtle, maybe with a slow animated offset for a slight 'gritty' shifting feel; keep it cheap (draw a limited number of lines, not per-pixel noise).
   - Draw all branches: for each branch, only draw the portion up to growProgress (interpolate current tip along its quadratic curve control point), use ctx.strokeStyle mixing branchColor/accentColor per branch's colorMix, ctx.lineWidth = its width, ctx.shadowBlur = a base glow amount (e.g. 8-14) with ctx.shadowColor matching the stroke color, use quadraticCurveTo with the branch's control point and end point for organic curves.
   - Draw synapses: small glowing circles/short glow strokes at synapse midpoint or connecting both tips with a very short curve, color synapseColor, ctx.shadowBlur = params.synapseGlow (brighter than branch glow), maybe a slow sinusoidal pulsing brightness using pulsePhase += dt.
   - Draw pulses: small bright dot (color pulseColor) at interpolated position along its synapse's path, ctx.shadowBlur scaled by params.pulseBrightness*some base, radius small (2-4px), and optionally a short fading trail (a couple of previous positions with lower alpha) drawn cheaply (no full particle system, just 1-2 trail segments).
   - Draw a vignette: radial gradient from transparent center to dark/black edges drawn on top with globalCompositeOperation multiply or just alpha black, covering canvas edges only.
   - Reset ctx.shadowBlur = 0 after each glow-drawing group to avoid leaking glow into unrelated draws (performance + correctness).

7. MAIN LOOP: use requestAnimationFrame with delta-time calculation (in seconds, clamp dt to avoid big jumps e.g. min(dt,0.05)). If params.paused, still render current frame (no time-based updates) but do not advance growth/pulses — just draw static state; when resumed, continue smoothly (reset lastTime on resume to avoid a huge dt jump). Each frame: if not paused -> update growth (if !growthDone), run checkSynapses periodically, update existing synapses' pulsePhase, spawn/update pulses; then always call render().

8. Wire up dat.gui color controllers' onChange callbacks to update the module-level color variables (backgroundColor, branchColor, accentColor, synapseColor, pulseColor) used by render(), so changing colors live-updates the visuals without needing regenerate. Wire the 'Regenerate Network' button to call createNetwork() (clearing old branches/synapses/pulses and growthDone flag, restarting growth animation). Wire 'Clear Canvas' button to empty branches/synapses/pulses arrays (network becomes empty, canvas goes blank aside from background/vignette/grid) without necessarily restarting growth (user can then hit Regenerate). Wire 'Pause / Resume' to toggle params.paused and correctly resume timing.

COMMENTS: Add short comments above each major section (SETUP, GUI SETUP, NEURON GROWTH, SYNAPSE DETECTION, PULSE ANIMATION, RENDERING, MAIN LOOP) explaining what it does, in plain generic technical language.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT reference any game, movie, brand, or copyrighted visual style anywhere in code or comments — keep all naming/comments purely technical (e.g. "neuron", "branch", "synapse", "pulse", "network").
- No images/textures/fonts loaded externally; only dat.gui via the one allowed CDN script tag.
- Keep code compact but readable; avoid heavy per-pixel noise loops; keep total branch/synapse/pulse counts capped for performance.
- The whole thing must be a single .html file with inline <style> and inline <script> (plus the one dat.gui CDN <script src> tag).

Generate the complete file content now."}
